jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at the University of Virginia (UVA) invites applications for multiple tenured or tenure-track faculty positions at all ranks.

We seek outstanding researchers and educators who will contribute to the continued growth, excellence, and intellectual breadth of the Department. The Department has substantial research strengths spanning artificial intelligence and machine learning, computer systems, architecture, cyber-physical systems, human-centered computing, robotics and autonomous systems, security, privacy, and cryptography, software engineering and programming languages, and algorithms and theory. We are particularly interested in candidates who will enhance and connect with the university’s AI research initiatives in both foundational and applied AI research, but also welcome applications across the full spectrum of computer science, including foundational research, emerging areas of computing, interdisciplinary research, and work that creates connections across established fields.

The primary responsibilities for these tenured/tenure-track positions include developing an internationally recognized research program, teaching and mentoring, and service to the department, university, public, and professional community. The appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Our department is proud of its strong culture of collaboration and collegiality and is committed to sustaining and strengthening it. Faculty collaborate extensively throughout the School of Engineering and Applied Science and with colleagues in UVA’s Schools of Data Science, Medicine, Nursing, Law, Public Policy, Business, Education, and Arts & Sciences. These connections foster opportunities for foundational and interdisciplinary research spanning computing, science, engineering, health, and society.

Computer Science plays a key role in several major interdisciplinary research efforts at UVA. The Department is a founding member of the Link Lab, a multidisciplinary research center bringing together researchers in computer science, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and aerospace engineering, and systems engineering to advance cyber-physical systems, robotics, autonomous systems, and the Internet of Things. CS faculty are also deeply engaged with UVA’s Biocomplexity Institute, university-wide efforts in artificial intelligence and data science, and interdisciplinary initiatives spanning health, biotechnology, neuroscience, and digital technology and society.

UVA is making substantial investments in computing and artificial intelligence research, including state-of-the-art high-performance computing and GPU infrastructure for large-scale AI, machine learning, data analytics, and computational science, and university-wide AI initiatives for researchers at all stages. These investments complement a growing university-wide community working on both the foundations of AI and its applications across science, engineering, health, and society.

The Department offers Ph.D. and master’s degrees through the School of Engineering and Applied Science and bachelor’s degrees through both the School of Engineering and Applied Science and the College of Arts & Sciences. Computer Science also collaborates with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering to jointly administer UVA’s undergraduate and graduate Computer Engineering programs.

UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution and one of the nation’s leading public universities. UVA is situated in the beautiful city of Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva .

In conjunction with these positions, senior graduate students are eligible and encouraged to consider the UVA Engineering Rising Scholars program. This program is designed to encourage early-career scholars to pursue a career in academia by supporting their postdoctoral work before beginning a tenure-track position at the University of Virginia. Detailed information and application instructions are available at https://engineering.virginia.edu/rising-scholars-postdoctoral-program

  

Candidates must have received a doctorate or equivalent in a computing field by the start of their appointment. Evidence of a commitment to high-impact scholarship, funded research, undergraduate- and graduate-level teaching and advising excellence, professional and university service, and mentoring are expected.

  

Applications should be submitted via Interfolio . Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026. The application package must include:

* a cover letter
* a curriculum vitae
* research statement
* teaching philosophy statement
* service statement
* three representative research papers;

In addition, the names and contact information of at least three individuals that can serve as references should be provided.

The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.

For questions about these positions, please contact Ferdinando Fioretto, Associate Professor, at fioretto@virginia.edu .

jobs.title: 4-H Youth Development Extension Agent - Club and Volunteer Development
jobs.description:
The WVU Extension Service is seeking a dynamic individual who will provide statewide leadership for 4-H Club and Volunteer Development programs. This position will lead efforts related to 4-H club development, volunteer management, compliance, chartering, special interest programs, volunteer training, program evaluation, and resource development. The position serves youth, volunteers, Extension professionals, and communities across West Virginia through educational programming, organizational development, and volunteer leadership initiatives. This is a statewide faculty position. The position carries the academic rank of Service Instructor or Service Assistant Professor, depending upon the candidate’s level of education. This is a twelve-month, full-time, promotable, non-tenure-track appointment.

**Major Responsibilities**

This position is primarily dedicated to serving youth, volunteers, communities, the state, the university, and the broader profession through the development, delivery, and evaluation of educational programs related to 4-H clubs, special interest programs, and volunteer development.

The successful candidate will provide statewide leadership for 4-H club and volunteer systems through educational programming, volunteer development, compliance oversight, partnership development, fiscal stewardship, and program evaluation.

The position is responsible to the State 4-H Program Director for all programmatic and administrative matters. The faculty member will work collaboratively with county Extension personnel, state Extension specialists, the WVU Extension Office of Volunteer Management, Compliance, and Development, community partners, and national organizations to strengthen and expand club-based and volunteer-led youth development programming throughout West Virginia.

**Functions and Tasks**

* Conduct educational programs in their designated program area to help people more effectively interpret and use science-based findings.
* Assume responsibility for developing, implementing, and evaluating a statewide Plan of Work for 4-H Club and Volunteer Development programming.
* Provides statewide leadership for 4-H club development, special interest programs, volunteer engagement, volunteer management systems, and organizational sustainability.
* Lead and coordinate statewide, interstate, and international 4-H youth development initiatives that promote leadership, citizenship, cultural competency, and community engagement.
* Collaborates with faculty, staff, volunteers, youth, and stakeholders to assess educational needs, identify priorities, and develop innovative educational opportunities that support statewide program goals.
* Review, revise, develop, and disseminate educational resources, curricula, and support materials for 4-H clubs, special interest programs, volunteers, and Extension professionals.
* Identify, recruit, train, support, and recognize volunteers who contribute to the successful delivery of 4-H club and special interest programming.
* Provide leadership for volunteer growth, retention, succession planning, and recognition initiatives across the state.
* Serve as the statewide leader for 4-H club chartering and Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) processes, ensuring compliance with established policies and procedures.
* Support youth protection and volunteer vetting processes in collaboration with the WVU Extension Vetting Team and the Office of Volunteer Management, Compliance, and Development.
* Plan, coordinate, and administer statewide contests, demonstrations, trainings, conferences, recognition events, and other program activities that advance positive youth development. This includes prominent events in Communication and Expressive Arts, fostering youth development.
* Develop and utilize effective systems for reporting program accomplishments, documenting outcomes, evaluating impacts, and demonstrating public value.
* Secure financial resources through grants, fundraising efforts, sponsorships, and partnerships to support program growth and sustainability.
* Provide leadership and guidance regarding fiscal management, tax exemption policies, financial accountability, and best practices for 4-H clubs and affiliated groups.
* Function at all times as a professional educator, maintaining high standards of teaching, scholarship, service, and stakeholder engagement.

**Service**

* Develop an understanding of the state, the needs of its citizens, and Extension’s role in meeting those needs.
* Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of youth development, volunteer engagement, organizational development, and community leadership needs throughout West Virginia.
* Serve as the statewide subject matter expert for 4-H club development, volunteer management, chartering, compliance, and special interest programs.
* Continuously evaluate and refine their role as an educator, leader, and change agent in strengthening volunteer-led youth programming across the state.
* Assess the degree to which programs meet the needs of youth, volunteers, Extension professionals, and stakeholders while promoting meaningful learning and behavioral change.
* Evaluate the effectiveness and impacts of educational programs and organizational systems related to clubs, volunteers, and youth engagement.
* Demonstrate the ability to apply current research, emerging trends, and best practices related to volunteer development, youth leadership, organizational management, and positive youth development.
* Work collaboratively with county Extension offices, schools, community organizations, state and federal agencies, and regional and national partners to strengthen programming opportunities.
* Serve as West Virginia’s liaison for regional and national initiatives related to 4-H clubs, volunteer development, and special interest programs.
* Participate in professional development activities that enhance expertise in youth development, volunteer management, educational program delivery, and organizational leadership.
* Provide mentorship and support to new Extension faculty and staff regarding effective club management, volunteer engagement, and program implementation.
* Support youth recruitment, retention, and student success efforts by creating educational experiences, workforce development opportunities, leadership pathways, and career exploration activities that encourage future enrollment at WVU and other post-secondary institutions.

**Teaching**

* Conduct needs assessments and engage community partners to identify priorities, mobilize resources, and develop, coordinate, and deliver research-based educational programs that meet the needs of citizens and communities.
* Develop, market, deliver, facilitate, and evaluate statewide educational programs focused on 4-H club development, volunteer leadership, organizational management, compliance, fiscal stewardship, and positive youth development.
* Establish clear educational objectives and utilize appropriate research-based subject matter and educational resources to achieve program goals and desired outcomes.
* Select, adapt, develop, and disseminate research-based curricula, training materials, and educational resources aligned with state and national 4-H priorities.
* Design and implement a variety of educational delivery methods, including trainings, workshops, conferences, webinars, volunteer development programs, and outreach activities to serve diverse audiences.
* Provide educational leadership and support to Extension professionals, volunteers, families, and community partners to ensure consistent and effective delivery of high-quality 4-H programming.
* Develop volunteer training and professional development opportunities that strengthen program quality, safety, accountability, and sustainability.
* Evaluate program effectiveness, measure participant outcomes and program impacts, and report accomplishments and public value to stakeholders and university leadership.
* Uses evaluation findings, stakeholder feedback, and emerging research to continuously improve program quality, relevance, accessibility, and impact.
* Understand the philosophy of Extension and utilize effective methodology in program delivery and evaluation.
* Understand and convey the philosophy, objectives and policies of WVUES.
* Assist in determining and obtaining resources needed to implement the Plan of Work.
* Plan and provide the training needed to equip volunteer leaders to carry out the program.
* Develop and maintain two-way communications with volunteer leaders.
* Understand and implement the provisions of EEO and ADA.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* For appointment at the Service Assistant Professor rank, the applicant must have a master’s degree.
* For appointment at the Service Instructor rank, the applicant must have a bachelor’s degree.
* Current West Virginia University faculty members who are selected for this position may be eligible to transfer their existing rank and tenure status, as appropriate and subject to University policies and procedures.
* Candidates with a degree in progress may be considered for this position, but the degree must be conferred by the hire date.
* Desirable areas of educational experience and training include youth development, Extension education, education, leadership studies, nonprofit management, community development, organizational leadership, public administration, agriculture, human services, or closely related fields.
* Demonstrated leadership and management skills through collaborations and partnerships with agencies and organizations is necessary.
* Documented experience in volunteer management, organizational development, program coordination, resource development, supervision, and team leadership is desirable.
* Proficiency in oral and written communication and knowledge and use of computer technology for educational programming and management are required.
* Experience working with advisory committees, focus groups, and volunteer organizations is desirable.
* Experience developing and delivering volunteer training programs is desirable.
* Experience working with the media and web-based information delivery methods is desirable.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Successful experience in developing financial support for educational programs through grant writing, fundraising, sponsorship development, contracting, or cost recovery efforts.
* Experience managing budgets, equipment inventories, and program resources.
* Extension or similar outreach education experience.

**Special Requirements:**

* Ability to meet travel demands of position (overnight stays), such as 4-H youth camps, conferences, professional development sessions and training.
* Willingness to work flexible hours, including nights and weekends.
* Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

**Position Assignment:**

* The Service Assistant Professor and/or Service Instructor positions are 12-month, full-time, non-tenure-track faculty positions.
* The successful candidate will be evaluated for providing a significant contribution in service and teaching. Accomplishments will be evaluated at least annually and will be judged in the context of these roles.
* The position will provide statewide leadership for 4-H club development, volunteer management, volunteer compliance, special interest programs, chartering and MOU processes, organizational development, fiscal stewardship, volunteer training, and related youth development initiatives.
* Salary: The fixed salary is $53,000 at the Service Instructor rank and $59,000 at the Service Assistant Professor rank.

**Application Process:**

* Applications will be reviewed beginning immediately and the search will remain open until the position is filled.
* If you meet the stated requirements and would like to be considered for the position, ALL of the following information must be submitted using https://careers.wvu.edu/career-opportunities:
  + Cover letter indicating the position that you are applying for and outlining experience and qualifications.
  + Resume or curriculum vitae including dates of employment, supervisor(s) name and contact information.
  + Three (3) references (including address, e-mail and phone) who can reflect on your professional strengths.
  + Transcripts (undergraduate and/or graduate). Degree must be conferred by start of position.

**About WVU Extension:**

WVU Extension is a primary outreach division of West Virginia University, embracing the heart of the University's land-grant mission. WVU Extension maintains a presence and connections in communities across all 55 West Virginia counties. It assesses local needs, seeks science-based best practices to meet these needs, and delivers educational programs and resources through several formal and informal systems. These connections are critical to the design, implementation, and evaluation of Extension and community engagement programs.

WVU Extension envisions a West Virginia where all its people can reach their fullest potential. Our mission is to improve lives and livelihoods of all West Virginians. Extension’s work is guided by collaboration and partnership; doing no harm; providing trusted, science-based practical education; helping people help themselves; serving all people, and exercising accountability. WVU Extension focuses on providing trusted and practical educational programs that improve health, education, and prosperity. These programs help people, businesses, and communities solve problems, develop skills, and build a better future.

WVU Extension is part of the National Cooperative Extension System present in every state and territory and is overseen by the USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA). It was created by Congress through the 1914 Smith-Lever Act. It is designed as a collaborative program funded through federal, state, and local match. WVU Extension also includes the Fire Service Extension (c. 1931), the Institute for Labor Studies and Research (c. 1959); the Occupational Health and Safety Extension (c. 1988), and the WVU Center for Community Engagement (c. 2021). Visit WVU Extension Service's website at https://extension.wvu.edu/ for additional information about our programs.

**About WVU**

West Virginia University is a place of purpose and community. We take pride in our profound impact on the state of West Virginia and are committed to the personal and professional growth of our employees.

From the groundbreaking R1 research at our flagship campus in Morgantown to the career-oriented programs at WVU Potomac State in Keyser, and the technology-intensive programs at WVU Tech in Beckley, the contributions of WVU employees resonate across the state, touching lives and shaping futures.

At WVU, you will discover a supportive community that champions work-life balance and fosters a collaborative atmosphere. Our core values — service, curiosity, respect, accountability and appreciation — unite us as Mountaineers.

Join us at West Virginia University, where your work will make a lasting impact. To learn more about WVU, visit wvu.edu.

West Virginia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or Veteran status.

jobs.title: Director of Collection & Resource Services and Assistant/Associate Professor - Odum Library
jobs.description:
**About Us**
------------

  

As a comprehensive institution of the University System of Georgia, Valdosta State University (VSU) is a welcoming, aware, and vibrant community founded on and dedicated to serving our communities' rich and diverse heritages. Through excellence in teaching, basic and applied research, and service, VSU provides rigorous programs and opportunities that enrich our students, our university, and our region. As such, the VSU mission consists of three interrelated parts that includes a student mission, university mission and regional mission. The university is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice civility, integrity and citizenship. As members of this community and proud Blazers we strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University, as stated in the Blazer Creed and reflected in our commitment to the University System of Georgia's Core Values.

**Blazer Creed**

Valdosta State University is a learning environment based on trust and mutual respect in which open dialogue, vigorous debate, and the free exchange of ideas are welcome. The University is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice **civility, integrity,** and **citizenship.** As members of this community, and proud Blazers, we will strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University.

**Civility** - A Blazer shows courtesy and compassion as well as respect for the dignity of every human being.

**Integrity** - Each Blazer is responsible for his or her own actions, and our community is stronger when we contemplate the context of our decisions and uphold the principles of trust and honesty.

**Citizenship** - Every Blazer has an interest in the well-being of the community, and, therefore, a duty to stay informed, to make positive contributions, and to offer support to those who need help.

As a Blazer, we pledge to uphold the core principles of **Civility, Integrity,** and **Citizenship**

**Job Summary**
---------------

  

Odum Library seeks qualified applicants for the Director of Collection and Resource Services, a 12-month tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, that begins as early as January 2027. Rank is determined at the time of hiring and will be commensurate with experience. The selected candidate will lead the Collection and Resource Services unit, be responsible for the acquisition and collection development of library collections, maintaining scholarly productivity, and participating in service at the college, university, state and/or national levels.

Review of completed applications will begin October 14, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. For more information on the position, contact Jessica Lee, Electronic Resources & Serials Librarian, via email at jessicalee@valdosta.edu.

**Application Process**

Online application is required. Applicants will be required to attach the following to their online application:

* CV
* Cover Letter
* Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
* Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least three references

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

  

**Typical Allocation of Duties****:**

25% Accomplish department/unit objectives
  
Direct the human, financial, and other resources needed to accomplish objectives of the department or unit.

20% Monitor and establish processes
  
Monitor and establish processes to ensure effectiveness, efficiency, and alignment with University and department goals.

20% Direct operations
  
Direct the operations of the department or unit.

15% Area Representative
  
Represent the department or unit to internal and external groups and individuals.

10% Manage budget
  
Manage the department/unit budget.

10% Compliance
  
Ensure commitment to and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and standards

**Supervisor Expectations****:**

**Director of Collection and Resource Services**

* Serve on the library's leadership team.
* Provide leadership and guide the direction for the following areas: acquisitions, collection development, cataloging, electronic resources.
* Supervise two faculty and four staff members.
* Lead initiatives that increase usability and make it easier for students to use resources independently.

**Acquisitions**

* Responsible for purchasing library materials including the acquisition and renewal of electronic database package subscriptions, individual serials, standing orders, books and other library materials.
* Create and update ledgers. Monitor expenditures in the integrated library system (Alma) and VSU fiscal systems and create reports as needed.
* Develop and maintain a positive working relationship with other campus entities including Procurement, Financial Services, and Budget Services.
* Establish and maintain vendor relationships, communicate needs, stay current with new products, product improvements, access and licensing alternatives.

**Collection Development**

* Coordinate collection development including reviewing usage of library resources, recommend adding or removing resources, and ensuring library collection supports curriculum.
* Prepare library portion of accreditation reports and meet with visitation teams.

**Scholarship, Professional Development, and Service**

* Maintain working knowledge of emerging trends in librarianship, acquisitions, and collection development.
* Engage in service at the library, the university, state and/or national level.
* Participate in scholarship, research, and/or creative activity. Contribute to the development of the library profession through scholarship, presentations, and publications.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Master's degree in library and information science from an ALA accredited program.
* Minimum of three years of progressive experience in cataloging, acquisitions, electronic resource management, or a related field in an academic library setting.
* Supervisory experience.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, organizational skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Familiarity with negotiating licenses and managing e-resources.
* Experience in maintaining effective relationships with vendors and participating in consortia purchasing agreements.
* Strong project management skills and attention to detail.
* Experience with the processes of procurement, contracts, or licensing.

**Proposed Salary**
-------------------

  

Commensurate with experience.

**USG Core Values**
-------------------

  

The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18\_personnel\_conduct.

Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.

**Conditions of Employment**
----------------------------

  

Applicants are required to provide:

* professional references with current contact information
* documentation of academic credentials
* employment history

Please note that during the search process, VSU reserves the right to:

* ask candidates who will serve in Positions of Trust to disclose criminal record history during the initial screening process and prior to a conditional offer of employment,
* view social media outlets, and
* remove job postings without additional notification.

Employment is contingent upon:

* successful completion of a background check investigation, including a criminal background check
* reference checks

Employment may also be contingent upon the job-based requirements if applicable for your position:

* satisfactory credit check
* successful completion of a Motor Vehicle Report (MVR)
* pre-employment drug testing
* confirmation of credentials

After initial hiring, employees will be required to successfully complete all of the following training:

  + Drug Free Workplace
  + Sexual Misconduct and Title IX
  + Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
  + Motor Vehicle Policy

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Valdosta State University is an equal opportunity educational institution. It is not the intent of the institution to discriminate against any applicant for admission, or any student or employee of the institution based on the age, sex, race, religion, color, national origin, disability, or sexual orientation of the individual.

Position of Trust + Credit

If you are a qualified individual with a disability, you may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to access job openings, apply for a job on this site, or participate in the search process as a result of your disability. You can request reasonable accommodations by contacting our Benefits Team, in the Office of Human Resources at vsubenefits@valdosta.edu

**Special Applicant Instructions**
----------------------------------

  

Valdosta State University may provide employment-based immigration sponsorship for select positions when consistent with institutional needs, University policy, and applicable law. Sponsorship is considered on a case-by-case basis and is not available for all positions. Applicants who anticipate requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future are encouraged to contact Human Resources early in the recruitment process with questions regarding sponsorship eligibility.

**Job Description:**
--------------------

The Department of Geography and Anthropology at Louisiana State University invites applications for a tenure-track **Assistant/Associate/Full** **Professor of Human Geography specializing in Geographic Information Science and Technology (GISc&T) and geospatial data science.** We seek a scholar with strong expertise in **GISc&T and advanced geospatial methods** to answer complex societal and human-environment questions.

Relevant methodological expertise may include spatial-temporal analysis, geospatial data science, remote sensing, GeoAI, WebGIS, geovisualization, or related computational approaches. Candidates are not expected to specialize in all these areas. We are particularly interested in candidates who can expand the department's methodological capacity and contribute to innovative applications of geospatial technologies in research and teaching.

The substantive area of specialization is open, but the successful candidate's scholarship must have a strong **human-geographic dimension**. Research areas may include, but are not limited to, health and well-being, population and inequality, food systems, energy and infrastructure, environmental change, hazards and disaster vulnerability, community resilience, critical GIS, or other societally relevant dimensions of human-environment interaction. We welcome scholarship that uses geospatial methods not simply as technical tools, but to advance understanding of important social, spatial, and environmental problems.

The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction in **GISc&T, spatial-temporal analysis, and environmental studies**, while developing courses in their areas of methodological and topical expertise. The position will also offer opportunities to contribute to and collaborate with the department's Environmental Studies and **Disaster Science and Management** areas and to strengthen interdisciplinary geospatial training across departmental programs in both geography and anthropology.

The successful candidate will be expected to develop an externally fundable research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses; mentor undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students; and contribute to the department's growing emphasis on interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholarship. Opportunities exist for collaboration across geography and anthropology and with programs and units throughout LSU, such as the South Central Climate Adaptation Science Center.

jobs.description:
The Rice School of Architecture invites applications and nominations for a full-time, tenure-track faculty appointment at the rank of assistant professor with a focus in architectural design, to begin fall 2027.

  

The Rice School of Architecture welcomes and promotes the productive interrelationship of design practice and scholarship and is committed to supporting and advancing the voices of architects in academia. We seek outstanding design faculty who will pursue a focused design research agenda in areas that may include, but are not limited to, representation, materiality, or environment, at scales ranging from the building to the city. Successful candidates will teach undergraduate and graduate design studios, offer lecture courses and seminars in their areas of expertise, and conduct research and produce creative work of the highest caliber. Faculty are expected to bring a distinct voice, develop and sustain a clear line of inquiry, participate in the collective intellectual conversation of the faculty, and contribute to the advancement of the field of architecture more broadly.

  

As the fourth-largest and one of the most dynamic cities in the United States, Houston, Texas reflects the world’s most pressing challenges and is an exciting laboratory for new forms of architectural discourse and design agency. The Rice School of Architecture draws upon this unique context and Houston’s immense arts, culture, and industry, offering opportunities for both local and global engagement. Furthermore, the school’s position within a top-tier research university allows us to collaborate with other disciplines to forge new territories of critical practice and innovation.

  

Candidates should hold, at a minimum, a master of architecture degree or its equivalent (degree requirements must be fulfilled by July 1 of the year employment commences). Applications should include a letter of interest describing the candidate’s teaching, scholarship, and creative work and how they situate their work within larger disciplinary conversations; curriculum vitae; research/practice portfolio highlighting design, research, creative practice, and writing (20MB max.); teaching portfolio with sample syllabi and student work (20MB max.); and contact information for three professional/academic references who may be asked to provide a written letter of reference if candidacy is advanced to the next stage of the search process. The Program in Creative Writing in the Department of English at The University of Alabama invites applications for two tenure-track Assistant Professors of English (Creative Writing, Open Genre) to teach in our thriving MFA program and undergraduate creative writing minor.

Our facilities and resources include state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and performance venues, providing students with hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for research and creative expression.
  
  
The College is committed to the liberal arts philosophy that fosters creative and critical thinking and a lifetime of learning.”

The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
  
  
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.
  
  
UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors.

UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year.
  
  
Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies.
  
  
The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. **Susan B. Meister Child Health Evaluation and Research (CHEAR) Center**
in the
**Department of Pediatrics**
at the
**University of Michigan Medical School**
is seeking applications for a
**full-time, faculty position at the Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor level on the instructional track (tenure track).**

is the oldest pediatric health services research center in the U.S. The Center includes 15 general pediatricians, pediatric subspecialists, economists, epidemiologists, and research scientists. Key strengths of the CHEAR Center include an interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, national reputation, strong administrative support, excellent research staff, longstanding relationships with the State of Michigan, and access to a broad range of administrative databases. Moreover, the CHEAR Center has access to the resources of the Institute for Healthcare Policy and Innovation, which unites 850 faculty across the University of Michigan who conduct health services research. The CHEAR Center and the University of Michigan are located in Ann Arbor, which is consistently rated as one of the best places to live in the U.S. by media outlets.

jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) and the Virtual Production Institute (VPI) invite applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track position in Interactive Spatial Audio and Multimodal Computing at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Visual Computing and Computational Media (VCCM) section. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

Candidates should demonstrate a strong potential for scholarly achievement and an ability to establish a nationally and internationally recognized research agenda. This position sits at the intersection of AI, multimodal computing, and audio and media technologies, with opportunities for research spanning computing, perception, and immersive systems. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to:

* 3D and Spatial Audio Rendering and Computational Acoustics

* Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Audio and Multimodal Computing

* Visual Computing and Multimodal Perception for Media and Entertainment, Simulation and Training, and/or Health and Wellness

* Interactive Audio Systems and Immersive Media for VR/AR/XR and Virtual Production

* Perceptual Evaluation and Psychoacoustics

* Hardware and Software Integration for Interactive and Multimodal Systems

* Audio Capture, Processing, and Sensing

* Audio Modeling and Synthesis; Multimodal Content Generation

The successful candidate will be expected to establish an active program of research, pursue external funding opportunities, disseminate work through publications, presentations, software systems, patents, or other recognized scholarly outcomes, and contribute to the national and international visibility of PVFA and the VPI.

The successful candidate will also be expected to teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, advise and mentor graduate students, including the Ph.D. in Visual Computing and Interactive Media program, participate in all aspects of PVFA’s and the VPI’s activities, and serve the professional community.

  

About the College

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. PVFA is built without departments. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. It operates at the main campus in Bryan-College Station and as part of Texas A&M – Fort Worth, with facilities equipped for work at the intersection of the arts and emerging technology. Applicants should consult the college's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/) to review our academic and research programs.

**About the** **Virtual Production Institute**

This position is aligned with the mission of the Virtual Production Institute. Formed in 2023, the VPI is a technology-focused ecosystem for teaching, learning, and research. It develops emerging applications and the skilled workforce needed for virtual reality, augmented reality, sensors, projectors, and computing across multiple disciplines and industries. Its facilities in Bryan-College Station and Fort Worth include a performance capture and sound stage with supporting technology studio classrooms. Applicants should consult the institute's website (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/institutes/vpi/).

Skaggs Presidential Chair in Nursing will execute a programmatic vision to strengthen the College and University of Utah Health Sciences' national and international presence and impact in acute and critical care research, practice, and education. Key responsibilities will include leading innovative research and scholarly activities; mentoring students, fellows and junior faculty; developing and teaching curriculum in the PhD, Doctor of Nursing Practice, and/or baccalaureate programs as aligns with the candidate's program of research and experience; engaging in professional service; and providing and/or consulting about acute and critical care. Collaborating with other leaders, the holder of the L. S. Skaggs Presidential Chair in Nursing will advocate for services and policy that benefit acute and critically ill patients and their families. The Chair will have opportunities to thrive in a collegial atmosphere that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration; fosters engagement with faculty and premier institutes and centers such as the Clinical & Translational Science Institute, Nora Eccles Harrison Cardiovascular Research & Training Institute, Huntsman Cancer Institute, Center for Genomic Medicine, Utah Data Coordinating Center, Scientific Computer and Imaging Institute, and Center for Health Ethics, Arts, and Humanities; and drives discovery with meaningful societal impact. College of Nursing faculty are expected to live in Utah.
  
  
Criteria
  
  
We seek a candidate who is a nationally recognized leader in acute and critical care, and whose accomplishments reflect excellence in acute and critical care research, scholarship, teaching, and clinical practice. Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in nursing or a related field from an accredited College or School and hold a current Registered Nurse (RN) or Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN) license or be eligible to obtain such. The ideal candidate will have a sustained record of externally funded research and evidence of high impact publications and presentations that pertain to acute and critical care nursing.
  
  
Appointment
  
  
The L. S. Skaggs Presidential Chair in Nursing is an administrative appointment, made by the Dean of the College of Nursing in accordance with University guidelines. The individual will maintain a tenure-line faculty position while in this role. Academic rank and salary will be commensurate with qualifications. A competitive start-up package is available to support the Chair's research and academic success.
  
  
**Responsible to:**
Chair, Division of Health Systems and Science across the Lifespan.
  
  
**Review and Evaluation:**
Formally reviewed every five years.
  
  
**College of Nursing**
The University of Utah College of Nursing is a premier nursing education institution with nationally ranked undergraduate and graduate programs. The College of Nursing prepares nurses at all education levels – BS, MS, DNP, and PhD – and has a current enrollment of more than 700 students. The College also offers an MS degree, undergraduate and graduate certificates, and an undergraduate minor in Gerontology.
*U.S. News & World Report*
rankings include: #6 Nurse-Midwifery program, #12 Online Master of Science in Nursing program, #22 Doctor of Nursing Practice program, and #39 Bachelor of Science in Nursing program.
  
  
With a $64M portfolio of grant funding, the University of Utah College of Nursing is consistently ranked in the top 20 in NIH funding among Colleges of Nursing. The College of Nursing is a focal point for clinicians and researchers to collaboratively design, lead, and achieve equitable improvements for the well-being of individuals, families, and communities. Our high priority research programs include the areas of social and behavioral aspects of chronic disease; innovative care delivery models; simulation in nursing and interprofessional education; social, behavioral, and environmental determinants of health and health equity science; and complement our strengths in women's health, aging, caregiving across the lifespan, informatics and systems science, and clinical and translational research. The Emma Eccles Jones Nursing Research Center provides unprecedented infrastructure and support for the College's research mission, and includes highly educated and trained pre- and post-award staff support, and a biostatistics core. Independent inquiry and collegiality form the fabric of everyday life for faculty and students.
  
  
The College of Nursing has 10 additional Chairs, and is home to the Family Caregiving Collaborative, Gerontology Interdisciplinary Program, College of Nursing Simulation Center, Center of Excellence for Exposure Health Informatics (CEEHI), Hartford Center of Geriatric Nursing Excellence, Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA)-funded Advanced Nursing Education Workforce (ANEW) program, and HRSA-funded Nurse Education, Practice, Quality & Retention (NEPQR) program. In 2017, the College of Nursing was the first recipient of the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN) New Era for Academic Nursing Award. The College also received the AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award in 2018. In collaboration with University of Utah Health (U Health), the college works to improve individual, family, and community health and quality of life.
  
  
**University of Utah and U Health**
The University of Utah (“the U”) – located in Salt Lake City, Utah – is an R1 university, member of the American Association of Universities, and member of the Big 12 Conference. University President Dr. Taylor Randall has a vision for the U to become a top 10 public university with unsurpassed societal impact, to grow to more than $1 billion in annual research expenditures, and to achieve an enrollment of 40,000 students. For the last 5 years, the U enrolled a record number of first-year students.
  
  
The University of Utah drives unsurpassed societal impact by preparing students from all walks of life to be leaders and global citizens who strengthen our society and democracy; generating and sharing new knowledge, discoveries, and innovations that supercharge our economy and improve lives locally, nationally, and globally; and engaging local, national, and global communities to promote education, health, and quality of life.
  
  
The Martha Bradley Evans Center for Teaching Excellence supports the University of Utah's mission and core values of student success and teaching excellence by 1) promoting engaging and transformational student learning experiences, 2) improving teaching effectiveness through evidence-based, equitable, inclusive, and anti-racist pedagogy, and 3) serving the needs of teaching-oriented faculty, instructors, and graduate students.
  
  
University of Utah Health – the only academic medical center in the Mountain West – includes numerous interdisciplinary entities such as the Huntsman Cancer Institute, the Huntsman Mental Health Institute, the Craig H. Neilsen Rehabilitation Hospital, the Nora Eccles Harrison Cardiovascular Research Training Institute, and the NIH-funded Utah Clinical & Translational Science Institute that support education, practice, and team science. With five hospitals, 12 community clinics, and a growing network of regional affiliates, U Health's catchment area covers five surrounding states, and roughly 10% of the United States.
  
  
Health Sciences schools include the College of Nursing, College of Health, College of Pharmacy, Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine, and School of Dentistry. The Spencer S. Eccles Health Sciences Library advances education, research, and health care through information access, service, and innovation, and serves the education, research, and clinical needs of faculty, scientists, health professionals, and students.

**Location:** Fairfax, VA

**Workplace Type:** On Site Required

**Sponsorship Eligibility:** Eligible for visa sponsorship

**Salary:** Salary commensurate with education and experience

**Criminal Background Check:** Yes

**About the Department:**

Mason’s Communication Department has a diverse and collegial faculty committed to excellence, innovation, community and public service, inclusion, and social equity. All department faculty participate in the life of our campus community, including career fairs, faculty functions, recruiting sessions and other events. Located just 15 miles from Washington, D.C., we offer a broad undergraduate program with more than 300 majors; six minor programs; a vibrant MA program including strategic communication; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; and media and culture specialties; and a highly ranked PhD program emphasizing health; strategic; and science, environment, and risk communication. The department also offers a graduate certificate in science communication. We serve a diverse population of undergraduate and graduate students who bring a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds to our classrooms. Additionally, the department supports several co-curricular activities, including debate, forensics, Public Relations Student Society of America (PRSSA), Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ), and a comprehensive student media program.
  
  
The research life of the department includes both undergraduate and graduate research and is reflected in the activities and outreach of its faculty, including those of the Center for Climate Change Communication (4C); the Communication, Health, and Relational Media (CHARM) research lab; the Center for Health and Risk Communication (CHRC); the Pop Culture lab; and the Character Assassination and Reputation Politics (CARP) research lab, in addition to several university-wide research centers and institutes including the Institute for Digital Innovation.
  
  
For more information on the Department of Communication at George Mason University, visit communication.gmu.edu.

**About the Position:**

The Department of Communication in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at George Mason University seeks a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication, with a specialty in new/emerging communication technology and innovative research methods.

Applicants should have a PhD in Communication or a closely related field. We welcome candidates from any communication subfield. We are especially interested in those whose work engages one or more of our core areas: strategic communication and public relations; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; media studies; journalism; or advocacy and political communication. The successful candidate will demonstrate an active research agenda focused on new/emerging communication technologies with innovative research methods, a record of competitive conference papers and/or scholarly publications commensurate with experience, an ongoing research agenda, a commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring a diverse student body, and a willingness to contribute to departmental and university service. We welcome all methodological approaches and specifically seek a candidate who pursues innovative methods to examine and/or utilize new and emerging technology. Candidates should demonstrate an ability to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in a variety of areas, as listed above. Overall, teaching experience at the university level is preferred. Finally, an interest in developing curriculum and courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels is also preferred.

**Responsibilities:**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in communication, including courses related to new and emerging technologies;
* Mentor and advise students;
* Develop and maintain an active research agenda focused on new and emerging communication technologies using innovative research methods; and
* Contribute to departmental, college, university, and professional service through committee participation, faculty governance, program and curriculum activities, and service to the discipline.

**Required Qualifications:**

* PhD in communication, or related field, completed prior to appointment;
* Active research agenda grounded in the study of new/emergent media, with a record of competitive conference papers and/or published research commensurate with experience;
* Demonstration of quantitative or qualitative innovative research methods, such as advanced natural language processing (NLP) and text mining (AI content analysis), digital ethnography, online social network analysis, AI content generation, social media analytics and big data analysis, agent-based modeling, or other innovative technological approaches to research;
* Ability to teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels that contribute to our subareas as listed above;
* Ability to teach theory courses in new media and technology and within the candidate’s particular subfield of communication;
* Commitment to teaching and mentoring a diverse student community; and
* Commitment to service for the department, university, and discipline.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* PhD in communication (rather than a PhD in a related field);
* A record of relevant published research commensurate with experience;
* Relevant teaching experience at the college or university level;
* Experience with or interest in developing courses and curriculum at undergraduate and graduate levels; and
* Experience with or interest in undergraduate student mentoring and graduate student advising.

**Instructions to Applicants:**

In a continuing effort to enrich GMU’s academic environment and provide equal educational and employment opportunities, we actively encourage applications from all job seekers.

For full consideration, applicants must apply at https://jobs.gmu.edu/; complete and submit the online application; and upload a CV, a cover letter describing their qualifications for the position, and a list of three professional references with contact information. For full consideration, please submit the above materials to GMU’s jobs portal (https://jobs.gmu.edu/) by November 30, 2026. The jobs portal will remain open until the position is filled.

**Posting Open Date:** October 9, 2026

**For Full Consideration, Apply by:** November 30, 2026

jobs.description:
**Description**
**About Arkansas Colleges of Health Education**
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE) is a private, non-profit, graduate-level health sciences institution located on over 500 acres in Fort Smith, Arkansas. ACHE’s service-driven mission is to educate and train a diverse group of competent and compassionate healthcare professionals; to create health and research support facilities; and to provide healthy living environments to improve the lives of others. Founded in 2014, ACHE has experienced rapid growth and is poised to be a leader in healthcare education for years to come. ACHE is the first and only private institution in Arkansas that is dedicated solely to healthcare and wellness, and maintains a strong commitment to the surrounding community.
  
  
**About Fort Smith And The Arkansas River Valley**
Fort Smith is a vibrant community of around 90,000, with a low cost of living and ample recreational opportunities. Located in the beautiful Arkansas River Valley at the foothills of the Ozark mountains, Fort Smith is nestled between the Ozark-St. Francis and Ouachita National Forests. The region provides hiking, mountain biking, rock climbing, hang gliding, whitewater rafting, and camping all within a short drive. In addition, the city supports a variety of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, an award-winning symphony, and two historic entertainment districts.
  
  
**LOCATION**
This is a hybrid position. The employee will be remote the majority of the time, with the supervisor determining any residential requirements.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL) Faculty member is a collaborative educator and scholar committed to excellence in graduate education, executive leadership development, scholarship, service, and continuous program improvement.
  
  
The faculty member will contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of the Doctor of Executive Leadership program through high-quality online instruction, curriculum development, student advising and mentorship, scholarly activity, program assessment, and institutional and professional service.
  
  
The faculty member will work collaboratively with the DEL Program Director, faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership to support the mission, vision, goals, and continued growth of the DEL program and Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE).
  
  
The faculty member will carry a teaching load as assigned based on program needs and institutional expectations and will actively contribute to the academic, scholarly, and service missions of ACHE.
  
  
**Essential Functions And Responsibilities**
**Teaching and Curriculum**

* Teach online Doctor of Executive Leadership courses within areas of demonstrated academic or professional competence.
* Provide high-quality, engaging, doctoral-level instruction appropriate for experienced working professionals and executive leaders.
* Develop, review, and revise course content, instructional materials, learning activities, and assessments.
* Ensure alignment among course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, instructional activities, and assessments.
* Maintain current, evidence-informed course content reflecting contemporary leadership theory, organizational practice, healthcare, business, policy, and other relevant areas.
* Utilize effective online teaching methodologies and educational technologies to promote student engagement and learning.
* Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic performance.
* Maintain consistent course organization, communication, grading practices, and academic expectations.
* Participate in continuous curriculum review and improvement.
* Support the development of new DEL courses, concentrations, certificates, educational pathways, and other curricular initiatives as assigned.
* Maintain the security and integrity of course materials, assessments, student information, and academic records.
* Teach courses in other ACHE programs when appropriate based on expertise and institutional needs.

**Student Advising and Mentorship**

* Serve as an academic advisor and mentor to DEL students as assigned.
* Maintain appropriate availability and responsiveness to students.
* Monitor student academic progression and provide guidance when academic or professional development needs are identified.
* Provide individualized mentorship that connects doctoral education with students' professional leadership goals and organizational impact.
* Support students experiencing academic difficulty and participate in remediation activities when appropriate.
* Refer student concerns involving academic performance, professionalism, or conduct to the DEL Program Director in accordance with institutional policies.
* Support student scholarly activities, presentations, publications, professional development, and other academic opportunities.
* Promote a supportive, inclusive, professional, and academically rigorous learning environment.

**Scholarship and Research**

* Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate to academic rank, professional expertise, and institutional expectations.
* Engage in research, applied scholarship, scholarly writing, peer-reviewed publication, professional presentations, or other recognized forms of scholarly activity.
* Pursue opportunities for collaborative scholarship with DEL faculty, ACHE faculty, students, and external partners.
* Mentor DEL students in scholarly inquiry, evidence-based leadership, research, and dissemination of scholarly work when appropriate.
* Participate in the development and evaluation of DEL program-related research and scholarly initiatives.
* Seek opportunities to translate research and professional experience into knowledge that advances executive leadership, organizational performance, healthcare, education, or other relevant fields.
* Pursue external funding, grants, or collaborative research opportunities when appropriate.
* Disseminate scholarly work at local, state, national, and international professional forums.

**Program Assessment and Continuous Improvement**

* Participate in the ongoing assessment and evaluation of the DEL curriculum and program.
* Assist with evaluation of course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, student performance, and other measures of program effectiveness.
* Participate in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of assessment data.
* Contribute to accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and continuous quality-improvement activities as assigned.
* Participate in periodic review and revision of course materials, curriculum, academic policies, and program processes.
* Provide recommendations to the DEL Program Director regarding opportunities to improve academic quality, student outcomes, and program effectiveness.
* Maintain required academic and administrative documentation in accordance with ACHE policies and applicable accreditation standards

**Program and Institutional Service**

* Serve as a member of DEL program committees and other ACHE committees as assigned.
* Participate in faculty meetings, curriculum meetings, assessment activities, retreats, and other institutional responsibilities.
* Participate in DEL admissions activities, including applicant review, interviews, and candidate evaluation as requested.
* Support DEL orientation, information sessions, recruitment events, student activities, and other program initiatives.
* Participate in faculty governance and institutional service activities consistent with academic appointment and institutional expectations.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff across ACHE programs to advance interdisciplinary education and institutional initiatives.
* Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of ACHE.
* Participate in commencement, academic ceremonies, institutional events, and other activities requiring faculty representation as appropriate.

**Recruitment and Program Growth**

* Support recruitment and enrollment initiatives for the DEL program.
* Participate in information sessions, webinars, conferences, professional meetings, and other recruitment activities as requested.
* Engage professional networks and organizations to increase awareness of the DEL program.
* Identify opportunities for educational partnerships, professional collaborations, and student recruitment.
* Support development of relationships with healthcare systems, academic institutions, professional organizations, government agencies, military organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other potential partners when appropriate.
* Assist in identifying emerging leadership-development needs and opportunities that may inform future DEL curriculum and program growth.

**Professional and External Engagement**

* Maintain active engagement within relevant professional and academic communities.
* Represent ACHE and the DEL program professionally at conferences, meetings, educational events, and community activities.
* Participate in local, state, regional, national, or international professional service appropriate to expertise and academic role.
* Develop relationships that may contribute to educational opportunities, research, scholarship, student development, or institutional partnerships.
* Maintain professional competence and remain current within areas of academic and professional expertise.

**Faculty Responsibilities And Professional Conduct**

* Maintain professional, ethical, and collegial relationships with students, faculty, staff, institutional leadership, and external partners.
* Demonstrate reliability, accountability, professionalism, and responsiveness in fulfilling assigned responsibilities.
* Adhere to ACHE policies and procedures and applicable academic, regulatory, accreditation, and ethical standards.
* Maintain confidentiality and privacy of student, faculty, and institutional information.
* Demonstrate respect for diverse perspectives, backgrounds, professional experiences, and areas of expertise.
* Contribute to a collaborative, solutions-focused, and professional faculty environment.
* Participate in faculty development and continuing professional education as appropriate.
* Complete required institutional training and administrative responsibilities in a timely manner.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the DEL Program Director, Dean, or their designee.

**Teaching Load**

* The DEL Faculty member will carry a teaching load as determined by the DEL Program Director and institutional leadership based on program needs, faculty workload expectations, areas of expertise, and other assigned responsibilities.
* Teaching assignments may include DEL courses as well as courses in other ACHE academic programs when appropriate, based on faculty expertise and institutional needs.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director, Doctor of Executive Leadership or their designee.

**Requirements**
**QUALIFICATIONS AND CREDENTIALS**
**Education And Experience**
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Earned doctoral degree from an appropriately accredited institution in leadership, healthcare, business, education, organizational leadership, public administration, or another field relevant to the DEL curriculum.

Hiring Department
  
  
Department of Veterinary Medicine & Surgery
  
  
**Job Description**
The
**College of Veterinary Medicine**
at MU is on a mission to educate and train outstanding clinicians and scientists, generate new knowledge, engage stakeholders, and foster economic growth, all of which promote and protect the health and welfare of animals and people. Our Doctor of Veterinary Medicine professional program boasts a unique curricular structure, which provides nearly two years of hands-on training in the college’s general and specialty clinics. Additionally, the College is a leader in the training of Undergraduate, Masters, and PhD students in the areas of Biomedical Sciences and Veterinary Pathobiology.
***Simply put, our mission is to Teach, Heal, Discover, and Serve.***
The
**Department of Veterinary Medicine and Surgery**
is dedicated to developing and disseminating knowledge to improve the health and well-being of animals and people through instruction, innovative research, service, and leadership. The department is home to the college’s
**Veterinary Health Center**
where our faculty provide clinical care, teach, and develop innovative treatments and therapies.
  
  
The
**Oncology Service**
in the MU College of Veterinary Medicine includes all three sub-specialties: medical, radiation, and surgical. The service is the second highest revenue generating service in our hospital, managing approximately 1,500 consultations every year. Comprised of four faculty members, the Medical Oncology team supervises six medical oncology residents annually, as well as contributes to the supervision and training of small animal rotating interns as well as oncology interns each year. In addition to patient care and treatment, house officer training, and DVM student education, the faculty in the service contribute to research activities both in the College of Veterinary Medicine, through public-private partnerships and clinical trials, and with the greater MU community through collaboration with the School of Medicine, the Ellis Fischel Cancer Center, and the NextGen Precision Medicine Initiative.
  
  
We are seeking an
**Assistant, Associate, or Full Tenure/Tenure Track Professor to join our Medical Oncology Service**
. Incumbents will be expected to maintain a strong caseload, participate in house officer training and DVM student education, as well as drive a robust translational research program that seeks to develop new and innovative treatments, improve diagnostic capabilities, increase patient outcomes, and drive understanding of cancer as a disease. They will be expected to participate in collaborative, interdisciplinary research efforts seeking to understand and treat cancer.
  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Provide high-quality treatment and patient care as a member of the medical oncology service.
* Participate in the clinical and didactic teaching of veterinary students; modeling professional conduct and providing case-based instruction and feedback.
* Train, mentor, and guide house officers (both residents and interns), providing consistent instruction, feedback, coaching, and mentoring.
* Build and maintain a strong research program in an area of Veterinary Medical Oncology. The University of Missouri places a strong focus on interdisciplinary and collaborative research and values a One Health and Comparative Medine mindset and approach to research.
* Contribute to and participate in college, departmental and hospital governance and service through committee work and other activities.

This is a full-time, benefit eligible, 12-month/year appointment. Distribution of effort between teaching, research, and service will depend on the career goals of the final candidate and the needs of the department.
  
  
***This faculty opening is cross-posted with a Non-Tenure Track (Teaching / Clinical) Faculty Position in Veterinary Medical Oncology (Job ID 60797). There is one opening that may be filled at any level depending on final candidate qualifications.***
**Qualifications**
**Minimum Qualifications:**

* A Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine (DVM) or equivalent degree (such as VMD, BVSc)
* Successful completion of a residency training program approved by the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine, Specialty of Oncology or the European College of Veterinary Medicine, Specialty of Oncology prior to appointment start date

**Candidates Will Be Evaluated On**

* Diplomate status or eligibility for board certification by ACVIM, Specialty of Oncology or an equivalent authority
* Possession of an advanced degree (Masters or Doctoral level) is required
* Professional, residency and graduate training
* Prior research productivity and experience building and maintaining an externally funded, independent research program
* Educational and professional achievement, career goals and the needs of the college
* Eligibility for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in Missouri, DEA registration and BNDD certificate

Application Materials
  
  
**Interested Candidates Should Be Prepared To Attach**

* Letter stating professional interests and career goals
* Curriculum Vitae

Please contact Noah Hartsfield, HR Recruiter, at hartsfieldn@missouri.edu or 573-882-3761 or Dr. Lee Talbott, Search Committee Chair at jtalbott@missouri.edu.
  
  
Sponsorship Information
  
  
Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.
  
  
Community Information
  
  
**MU is a nationally competitive, global university.**
Many states fund separate research and land-grant universities, but Missouri combines those roles at its flagship institution. MU is both a land-grant university with a statewide mission of service to citizens and Missouri’s largest public research university. Mizzou is one of only five universities nationwide that offers law, medicine, veterinary medicine, and a nuclear research reactor on one campus.
  
  
**About**
**MU is a national leader in comparative medicine,**
in which researchers collaborate by sharing discoveries, innovations and treatments for humans and animals. For more about the College of Veterinary Medicine and our impact on Missouri, the nation, and the world, go to:
  
  

* University of Missouri/College of Veterinary Medicine - http://cvm.missouri.edu/
* Veterinary Health Center - http://www.vmth.missouri.edu/
* Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Lab - http://vmdl.missouri.edu/

**Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and a high quality of life for people of all ages and interests.**
Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia is right in the middle of the state and the nation. Just a couple hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone County’s largest population center offering big-city culture, activities, and resources with a low cost of living. Columbia is home to a variety of restaurants and entertainment venues and hosts more than a dozen festivals each year. If you want to grow your career, continue your education, raise a family, and retire, Columbia is a good place to be!
  
  
Benefit Eligibility

Candidates for this position will be responsible for developing and maintaining a health services or other clinical research laboratory, engaging as principal investigators and collaborators in research and obtaining/maintaining independent extramural funding. This position will work closely with researchers and clinicians in the Division of General Internal Medicine (GIM), and will have the opportunity to interact with Department of Medicine and University of Wisconsin researchers. All Faculty: Teach medical students, residents, and fellows.
  
  
The selected candidate will be expected to engage in active collaborative research and obtain/maintain independent extramural funding. Through these efforts, the applicant will enhance national recognition for our division
  
  
**Department:**
School of Medicine and Public Health / Department of Medicine, Division of General Internal Medicine.
  
  
The University of Wisconsin-Madison in one of the 10 largest research institutions in the country, allocating more than $1 billion annually to groundbreaking exploration. This position will be located within UW-Madison’s School of Medicine and Public Health. The Department of Medicine, the largest department in the school, empowers leaders to transform medicine. The department includes 11 divisions, and was ranked 25th in the country in extramural grant funding in FY25, with $152 million in extramural grants. We are experts in ambulatory education, population health and chronic medical care for complex patients—and we work in partnership with our world-class university and remarkable health system. Our faculty lead their own highly collaborative clinical and dissemination and implementation research laboratories (https://www.medicine.wisc.edu/general-internal-medicine/research-division-general-internal-medicine).
  
  
In addition, several members of our division are affiliated with the Center for Tobacco Research and Intervention. Federally funded for over thirty years, the center performs ground breaking tobacco research https://ctri.wisc.edu/ With Family Medicine and Pediatrics, we mentor research fellows through the HRSA funded T32 Primary Care Research Fellowship (https://www.fammed.wisc.edu/fellowships/primary-care-research/).

Negotiable, 12 month

* SMPH Faculty /Academic Staff Benefits Flyer 2026
